claims.text: HEA protective-coating wear performance is primarily governed by formation of a nanocrystalline microstructure during deposition.
A nanocrystalline microstructure enhances coating hardness.
A nanocrystalline microstructure increases resistance to plastic deformation.
Changing substrate temperature or deposition rate can promote nanocrystalline structure formation in a PVD-deposited HEA coating.
A nanocrystalline microstructure has a higher grain-boundary density than a coarse-grained microstructure.
Grain boundaries act as barriers to dislocation motion in the HEA coating.
Restricted dislocation motion enhances the hardness of the HEA coating.
Restricted dislocation motion enhances the wear resistance of the HEA coating.
Nanocrystalline HEA coatings will have lower wear rates than coarse-grained HEA coatings under identical sliding-wear conditions.
Nanocrystalline HEA coatings will have higher hardness than coarse-grained HEA coatings.
The proposed relationship should hold for coating grain sizes from 10 to 100 nm.
The proposed relationship should hold under moderate loads and sliding speeds typical of industrial applications.
Chemical composition, oxidation resistance, and secondary phases may also influence wear performance.
